subject: zoology_2
question_text: Mention the names of any four connecting links that you have studied.

verification.note: Sourced from 'My Baby Bullet-Q — Senior Inter Zoology' (Star-Q Pass Track Series, Sri Publishers, 2022), book p.57, VSAQ 118. The printed exam years are the book's claim, reproduced here as appearances. Zoology-II holds only ONE source book in the corpus, so the two-book union check is structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is our reading of the question and is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. Revised 2026-09-05 after the examiner audit: the question asks only for names, so the insider note and the first common mistake no longer treat a bare list of four correct names as an error.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Two connecting links
steps.why: A connecting link shows features of two groups at once, so it is evidence that one group gave rise to the other.
common_mistakes: Naming an animal that is not a connecting link.
Naming Archaeopteryx as a link between amphibians and reptiles.
steps.margin_note: Write each name with its two groups.

steps.label: Two more
steps.why: Archaeopteryx had feathers like a bird and teeth like a reptile, which is exactly what a connecting link means.
common_mistakes: Giving only three links when four are asked.
Placing Cynognathus between birds and mammals.
steps.memory_tip: Archaeopteryx to birds, Cynognathus to mammals.
steps.margin_note: Four named links complete the answer.

insider_note: The question asks for four names, and four correct names answer it. Write the two groups each one joins beside the name as well — it takes only a few extra words and shows that you know why the animal is a connecting link.
